title: Squares inside rectangles
notes: Keep one adult at each table; outlined squares can replace cutting, as on guide p1. On return, K-1 can use identical squares (P4) or make every rectangle from four supplied tiles (P5). Grades 2-3 can connect the last square to equal-square coverings (P3-5), then invent rectangles sharing a last size (P6). Grades 4-5 can justify the common-divisor invariant (P4-5) or pool the bounded most-sizes search (P6) across pairs. Keep each square-size list with its starting rectangle.

For the optional four-square task, sixteen matching 3-by-3 cutouts give each of four children a set; eight suffice for two pairs sharing. Drawing square boundaries remains the low-preparation alternative. Keep grid and cutout scales matched.
